summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored UK Tier 1 (Investor) documents: Home Office statistics (entry clearance tables to 2018, extensions and settlement datasets to 2025, settlement tables 2008-2018), the MAC 2014 report, statements of changes HC 863/HC 693/HC 1025/HC 1919/CP 632, written statements and answers, the closure press release and the ISC Russia report. Every Investor cell of the Home Office tables is now taken (extensions by nationality, quarter, applicant type and outcome 2010-2025; settlement by nationality 2008-2018 and 2020-2025; quarterly entry clearance applications and outcomes 2008-2018). 6531 new observations, 21 rule rows, 0 events (all events already in the data), 3 new indicators (plus 2 shared with other passes).

new_indicators.name: Programme holders switching to another immigration route

ledger.contains: Statement of Changes CP 632 (12 pp.): implementation at 16:00 on 17 Feb 2022; review clause; changes to Part 6A closing Tier 1 (Investor) to new applicants (extension applications only by people holding Investor leave now or in the last 12 months, before 17 Feb 2026; entry clearance and leave to remain granted for 2 years; settlement applications before 17 Feb 2028) and consequential changes to Appendix A (Table 7 deleted). No statistics. Closure and 2026 deadline events already in the data; added one rule row (2-year grant period after closure).

Explanatory memorandum to CP 632 (4 pp.): closure with immediate effect, departing from the 21-day convention to avoid a 'closing down sale'; reasons (small economic benefit, illicit wealth, complex schemes); cites MAC 2014 (threshold raised from GBP 1m to GBP 2m, rules already recorded from HC 607/HC 693), a Home Office review of a sample of extension applications granted in 2019 (no numbers given) and the ISC Russia report; Innovator reforms planned for autumn 2022; no regulatory impact. No programme statistics. Closure event already in the data.

Extensions detailed datasets, year ending June 2026. Data_Exe_D01: grants and refusals of extensions of stay by quarter, nationality, applicant type (main/dependant) and category, 2010 Q1-2026 Q2; the Investor subgroup has 2,896 non-zero cells (2010 Q1-2025), all now taken (2,661 grants as residence_permits_renewed, 235 refusals as residence_renewals_refused). Data_Exe_D02: grants to main applicants by current and previous category of leave, 2015-2025: Investor renewals (previous Investor, 2015-2024) were already in the data; now added the 66 rows of in-country switches into Investor by previous category (incl. 2025, previous 'Unknown', 58) and the 26 rows of Investor holders switching to other categories 2015-2020 (new indicator programme_switches_out). Pivot sheets Exe_D01/Exe_D02 repeat the data sheets. All other categories (other routes) are out of scope. No printed totals for Investor in the data sheets, so no sum check was possible.

Statement of Changes HC 1025 (243 pp. incl. explanatory memorandum). Investor parts: paras 110-117 (minimum age 18, study condition), Appendix A paras 268-283 (Table 7 with GBP 2m and a UK regulated bank account, bank letter, 90-day funds evidence, property-company exclusion, maintaining and reinvesting the portfolio within 6 months, fees from surplus), EM para 7.37. Took the minimum age rule (18 from 6 Apr 2015; 16 before). The bank-account rule is already an event; GBP 2m threshold already a rule from HC 693. The GBP 2.1m/GBP 100,000 example in para 280 is an illustration, not a rule. The rest of the statement concerns other routes (out of scope).

Explanatory memorandum to HC 1919 (19 pp.). Investor parts paras 7.20-7.27: GBP 2m minimum; funds-holding period extended from 90 days to 2 years; bank due-diligence confirmation; UK government bonds excluded; FCA regulation of intermediary vehicles; 'active and trading' tightened; pooled investments with UK government funding allowed; transitional protection to 5 Apr 2023 (extensions) and 5 Apr 2025 (settlement); extension entry clearance period 2 years 4 months; refusal grounds extended; old transitional arrangements closed from 6 Apr 2020/2022. Took 2 rule rows (2-year funds rule, 2y4m extension grant); reform event already in the data. Other content (Start-up, Innovator, EU Settlement Scheme with its own application counts, Tier 2, stateless leave) is out of scope.

Statement of Changes HC 693 (93 pp. incl. EM). Investor parts: refusal grounds on source of funds (para 245EB), extension capital GBP 2m / GBP 750,000 by entry date (para 245EE(e)), Appendix A Tables 7, 8A, 8B, 9A, 9B (GBP 2m fully invested; old GBP 1m/GBP 750,000 and loan options kept for pre-6 Nov 2014 entrants; settlement after 2/3/5 years at GBP 10m/5m/2m), EM para 7.25. Thresholds and the loan-option removal were already rule rows; added the three settlement qualifying periods. The transitional ILR loan option thresholds (GBP 20m/10m/2m personal assets) are restatements of the old rules. Other routes out of scope.

Statement of Changes HC 863 (67 pp. incl. EM). Investor parts: new para 245EF (ILR), Appendix A Tables 7-9 (GBP 1m own money or GBP 1m loan with GBP 2m assets; 75% (GBP 750,000) in qualifying investments; ILR after 2/3/5 years at GBP 10m/5m/1m; absences up to 180 days in 12 months), EM paras 7.8 and 7.16 (initial leave raised from 3 years to 3 years 4 months; 90-day funds rule brought into the Rules; no annual limit). Accelerated-settlement thresholds were already rule rows; added settlement qualifying periods (3), the 180-day absence limit, the 3y4m initial leave and the 90-day funds-holding rule. Other routes out of scope.

Written statement of 6 Dec 2018 announcing Start-up and Innovator routes and that the Tier 1 (Investor) route will be reformed in spring 2019 (event already in the data). No Investor numbers; the rest concerns other routes (Exceptional Talent, Tier 5 religious and charity workers, seasonal workers pilot).

Written statement of 12 Jan 2023 on the review of Tier 1 (Investor) grants 30 Jun 2008 - 6 Apr 2015: 6,312 main applicants and adult dependants reviewed (already in data); refusal rates 7.9% entry clearance, 4% leave to remain, 2.2% settlement (already in data); 10 oligarchs who used the route sanctioned (added as high_risk_applicants_identified); GBP 1m threshold at launch and the 1994 predecessor (rules already recorded); systemic findings (no numbers). The figures on all UK Russia sanctions (1,200 individuals, 120 entities, over GBP 18bn frozen) are not about the route and are not recorded. Events already in the data.

Home Office press release of 17 Feb 2022 announcing the closure of the Tier 1 Investor route with immediate effect, with a quote from the Home Secretary and a promise to publish the 2008-2015 review. No numbers about the programme; the closure is already recorded as an event from the CP 632 explanatory memorandum.

Written answer of 18 Apr 2018 on politically exposed persons: Home Office does not hold PEP data in collatable form; thresholds GBP 1m before 6 Nov 2014 and GBP 2m since (added as 2 rule rows); refers to the Home Secretary's 28 Mar 2018 commitment to review the route (event already in data).

Written answer of 21 Apr 2022: as of 19 Apr 2022, 10 sanctioned Russian nationals had held Tier 1 (Investor) leave, 7 of them with an initial or further grant after 2014. Both numbers added (high_risk_applicants_identified); event already in data.
Written answer of 13 Mar 2023: the review covered 6,312 applicants and adult dependants (already in data); declines to give risk counts or countries.
Written answer of 17 Sep 2014: Tier 1 Investor visas granted to Russian main applicants, 501 in April 2010 - June 2014 and 119 in January-June 2014 (both already in data); refers to table vi_06_q_w.

Settlement detailed datasets, year ending June 2026. Data_Se_D01: grants of settlement by year, nationality and category 2020-2025; all 234 'Investor (previously Tier 1)' cells now in the data (210 added; China, Russia, USA and Hong Kong were already there). Se_D02 (quarterly, by applicant type) has only the broad 'High value' category, so nothing Investor-specific; Se_D03 (sex and age) has no category split. Notes say dependants are under 'Family' in Se_D01. No Investor total row is printed, so no sum check was possible. Other categories out of scope.

Settlement tables, year ending Dec 2019 (se_01 to se_06). Only se_03 has an Investor column ('5 years aggregate of pre PBS categories and Tier 1 High Value Migrant Investors'), by year 2004-2018 (2004-2007 printed 'z'), world region and country of nationality. All printed cells for 2008-2018 now taken: yearly totals were already in data; added the region subtotals and every country cell (including printed zeros), 2,475 rows. Check: for every year the countries add up to their region subtotal and the regions add up to the printed total. se_01, se_02, se_02_q, se_04, se_05 and se_06 have no Investor category (out of scope).

Entry clearance visa tables, year ending Dec 2018. vi_04 (annual grants by category, main applicants and dependants 2008-2018) was already in the data. Now added vi_04_q (quarterly grants 2008 Q3-2018 Q4, main and dependants) and vi_01_q (quarterly applications, resolved, granted, % granted, refused, % refused, withdrawn, lapsed for Tier 1 - Investors, main and dependants, 2008 Q2-2018 Q4; 2008 Q2 has applications only). Checks: quarterly grants add up to the annual vi_04 figures for every year; resolved = granted + refused + withdrawn + lapsed in every quarter; vi_01_q granted equals vi_04_q. vi_02_q, vi_03, vi_05 and vi_05_q are by nationality for all categories with no Investor split (out of scope).

Home Office 'Why do people come to the UK? To work', year ending March 2022. Section 1.1: 820 Investor grants (year ending Mar 2022), 726 (year ending Mar 2020), 221 Chinese, 86 Russian, 85 US nationals (all already in data); the '13% higher' is the change between two recorded values and is not recorded separately; section 2.1 dates the closure. The rest (Skilled worker, Global Talent, Innovator, Entrepreneur and other routes, labour market) is out of scope.

Intelligence and Security Committee report 'Russia' (HC 632, 2020). Paras 49-50 and 56: the investor visa scheme (from 1994) as key to London's appeal for Russian oligarchs; recommends an overhaul of the Tier 1 (Investor) programme (event already in data). Footnote 60 restates the rules (3 years 4 months for a GBP 2m investment), already recorded from HC 863/HC 693. No programme statistics; the rest of the report is out of scope.

MAC report 'Tier 1 (Investor) route: investment thresholds and economic benefits' (Feb 2014, 108 pp.). Ch. 1: call for evidence (25 organisation and 12 individual submissions; Annex A says 10 individuals; ~200 investors contacted; calls with 4 investors). Ch. 2: rules and history (thresholds, settlement and citizenship periods, Table 2.2), Home Office grant data: Table 2.3 out-of-country and in-country grants (main/dependants) YE 2009 Q3-2013 Q3, Table 2.4 top-10 nationalities 2008 Q3-2013 Q3, refusals, in-country cumulative grants, Table 2.5 previous visa types 2011-2012, age shares and average ages, dependant ratios. Ch. 3: investment of about GBP 500m a year, Table 3.1 living expenditure, Table 3.2 spending and taxes per investor, professional-services fees, 638 dependant children, partner survey shares. Ch. 4: 90-100% invest the minimum, Tables 4.1-4.3 on other countries. Ch. 5-6: inflation-uplift thresholds (GBP 1.9m/2m/1.8m), recommendations (GBP 2m minimum; auction of about 100 premium visas with a GBP 2.5m reserve incl. a GBP 500,000 gift; 90-day residence), Table 6.1. Added 97 observations (all remaining UK route numbers above, with Table 2.4 and Table 3.2 parts checked against their printed totals) and 5 rule rows; 29 rows were already in the data. Single-case anecdotes (one investor's GBP 23,000 school fees, a client spending GBP 14m on property, a GBP 50m purchase) and macro context (deficit, gilt market size, ISC pupil numbers, London property inflows, gilt yields) are not programme statistics and are not recorded. The MAC recommendations and the Mishcon de Reya GBP 1-2bn claim for a hypothetical GBP 20m route are proposals, not recorded as numbers (the recommendation is covered by the existing event).
